I tried to like this game. I really did... It's just not my cup of tea. I thought it would be a "Midnight Diner" coffee version. 

The espresso making game is cool. 

I just wish there was more of a choice than just making the wrong espresso.

A visual novel first and a coffee shop simulation second. I was hoping I'd be more of a barista than a personal therapist. Nevertheless, I should've guessed based on the title, so that's on me. 

Relaxing pace and atmosphere, but those weren't enough to save it from the sleep-inducing storyline, which is not as mature as I'd have liked. On the flip side, one might find it relatable since the issues presented were, frankly, common and unremarkable, in a sense that there wasn't enough hook and/or suspense to maintain my interest.

Terribly boring. Nearly zero actual gameplay, and the story isn't interesting enough to make up for the fact that you're just staring at your screen for hours on end, listening to customers complain about their lives, and waiting for the few moments you click buttons to "make" a beverage. You can't make a single mistake or you have to reset to get all of the achievements, and to add insult to injury, the "Art Takes Time" achievement wasted far more than one hour of my life.
Very weak writing and pretty much no real gameplay.

At first I really loved this game. The art, the music, the characters. What I didn't like (and what made me quit the game without finishing) is trying to figure out how to brew the correct drinks for the customers. I didn't want to use a guide, but for me that's the only way I was going to be able to finish.  I might come back at a later date using a guide, but right now I'm too frustrated to want to play.

Wanted to like this one, but the writing was just so stilted and cliche. Even for a visual novel the gameplay is drab, I found myself putting auto-text on and just scrolling on my phone like the customers were. The atmosphere is also non-existent, both for the coffee shot and the PNW. It just feels like the developers decided they had to put the coffee shop in Seattle, because Seattle is known for rain and coffee and that would give them the "vibes" they wanted.

The art is very pretty but I'm sorry I did not like it. Maybe it's just not for me. I played a bit less than an hour and found the dialogues and the stories... stale, and boring. The thing I liked the most about it is the actual coffee making process, which is about 10% of the actual game. Initiated a refund. Sorry

gameplay is fun and the game is great, but no sex 0/10
Wanted a game with more talking/dialogue options. This game is fine and I get why others like it but personally just not for me.

This game feels like routinely watching state propaganda on TV that you already agree with if you're an American millennial democrat. Baffling for someone not a part of American culture, it's like the devs just wanted to virtue signal. The hyperfixation on racial issues seems outright racist for an outsider looking in.

This game isn’t bad—it’s just not very satisfying.
The soundtrack and pixel art are good, creating a cozy atmosphere.
But if you're drawn to the idea of brewing coffee, you might feel a bit disappointed. All you do is press buttons, and the latte art gameplay feels stiff.
Also, the story is predictable. You can guess how things will unfold early on, and by the end, 95% of your predictions will come true.
There was potential in these areas to make it better, but the game falls short.
Ultimately, this is more of a visual novel than a game. You have very limited control over the ending. You simply witness the story, and that’s it.

The story was boring and a bit weird. Without any meaningful gameplay, the lack of story started to bug me. Also, the final plot twist was really irrelevant to the things that had happened in the game.

The Good:
The characters all have deep stories and character progression.
The Bad:
I suck at making coffee. Why can't these people just tell me what they want so I can make it correctly and they'll stop hating me. Also, the main person with the green hair irks me so much. I do not care about them and I want them to leave my coffee shop. It's repetitive and a little boring and I don't care about these people. I just skip their dialogue until Hyde comes in cause I'm a fiend for vampires but then Hyde asks for something I don't know how to make and I cry.
The Ugly?:
I don't like the way they look at me.
I recommend this game to people who like to read and enjoy visual novels.

Boring game, too much talking instead of making coffee.
Mid stories. Mid characters. Coffee talk? more like Coffee YAPPING
more of a visual novel..... better coffee sims out there

Well, I enjoyed the opening of the game and making my first cup of coffee. Also, the user interface with its sliding panels was delightful. However, beyond my initial impression there just wasn't anything of substance here. 

The coffee brewing seems to stick to a 1, 2, 3 pattern, which is perplexingly simple. Figuring out the Latte-Art functionality was actually more challenging than any of the brewing. (post-game edit: in all fairness, the complexity of coffee brewing increases in later stages of the story mode by making you guess unknown drinks)

The music was average. There a whole lot of tracks offered via the smartphone but none of them really helped to enhance the mood and quickly became a distracting background noise.

The writing is, I am sorry to say this, boring, shallow and simply not good. So much so, I found myself wishing to be able to wipe the counter, do the dishes, anything else but being locked into listening to a werewolf and a vampire ramble on about something I had absolutely no stake in. I even opted to just skip that conversation hoping to get to make another simplistic coffee but when it took a minute of fast double-clicking my way through a surprisingly large amount of uninteresting text I just knew this game and its writing isn't for me. 

Sorry, but I am not recommending this.

---

Addendum: Okay, okay. It's a calm Saturday morning, I brewed myself a nice cup of coffee, put on some Japanese City Pop, in the options I disabled the grating BGM, enabled the Fast Forward option for all speech and hey, the game wasn't so bad. To be honest, I still skipped all of the writing to do the stuff I personally enjoyed, which was figuring out the drinks based on hints and enjoying the pixel-art. Once you are through the story mode you unlock a challenge mode as well as a gallery with a lot of art from game development. I enjoyed both of those things, so thank you for that!

I think Coffee Talk has redeemed itself with me, but I will leave this on 'Do not recommend' due to the very repetitive music tracks (seriously, turn it off and listen to something you like) as well as the, again sorry, mediocre writing I experienced in the first 2 days of the story.

After playing that other game, I came here with really high expectations. And don't get me wrong: the art, the music and the UI are all top-notch, a significant upgrade over Coffee Talk's spiritual ancestor.

Here's the thing, though: if a game with barely any gameplay wants to shine, its writing needs to be [i]outstanding.[/i] It needs to have a gripping plot, intriguing characters and witty dialogue. Whereas in Coffee Talk, story-wise, we have (go on and open the spoiler, it's nothing special):

[spoiler]- A storyline about a writer who writes a novel, finishes it, and that's it;
- Another one about a werewolf who hangs out with a vampire, then turns into a wolf and back into a human, and that's it;
- Yet another about an elf and a succubus who want to be together but don't want to break up with their families, so they have a falling out, then meet again and get back together, and that's it;
- Yet another one about two game developer girls who hook up in the coffee shop, and that's it;
- Yet another one about a young singer who rebels about her dad and joins the bad crowd but then he protects her against that crowd and she makes up with him;
- The final one about an alien who wants to procreate with Earthlings but then leaves, and that's it.[/spoiler]

You should see what's wrong here: only one of these storylines (the one with the singer) is a storyline in its own right, with a plot, culmination and denouement. The rest are barebone snippets that have little substance and don't go anywhere.

The characters are a very subjective matter, but I personally didn't see a single one that would make me like or care about them. The back-and-forth between the werewolf and the vampire was the most promising one in terms of character development, but once again, it was too little, too late.

As for the actual text...

"Oh, Aqua! Fancy seeing you again so soon."
"Hi, Freya."
"Hi, Barista."
"Good evening, Miss Aqua."
"How are you two doing?"
"Same old."
"I'm good, how about you?"
"I'm fine, thank you, and you?"
"Oops!"
"I asked that already!"
"I'm sorry."
"Don't worry about it."

I'm not making this up. These are twelve lines of actual in-game text that should have been edited down to zero. I'll admit this is a bit of cherry-picking: it's not this egregious most of the time. But the amount of empty placeholder banter is so high that this little three-hour game should be at least 30% shorter.

To summarize, I find very little to like here in terms of story. By the way, did you know that the word "story" is repeated 38 times across the game? "There's so many stories this coffee shop has", "These people have stories to tell..." - the game drones on and on from the beginning. 

But when it comes to actual content, it's lukewarm 3-in-1 instant coffee quality at best.

Really just wanted a lo-fi version of the cyberpunk Va11-ha11a. I really wanted to like this, but the characters and the writing didn't really grab me. The world and the people just aren't nearly as interesting and they have to be really strong to carry a game like this that's literally 100% conversations and experiencing the world outside through characters. 
Just falls short of the mark in some aspects for me, it just never grabbed me. 

It is deeply upsetting that the writer will never get another chance to iterate on this formula that they were very passionate about, but hopefully the rest of the studio can carry on in his memory and make something truly incredible.

I can't recommend this game, sadly. It gets caught between two serious gameplay design choices that bother me a lot because it needed to commit but it didn't, so you get a lukewarm coffee experience. 

In my opinion, you needed to be a completely passive listener/barista, almost eavesdropping or overhearing people's lives, and still keep the coffee mechanic. If you're thinking, that doesn't sound like a game, well, you've got it. There are dialogue options but they really don't matter, which leads to the alternate route the game could have gone:

Your dialogue options ACTUALLY make a difference, and you can get different outcomes and shape characters/story/plot/etc. 

Instead, this game feels like a visual novel with not enough agency, but it's not passive enough for you to feel like you're getting a glimpse into "the lives of others." So instead, you're left with a middle of the road feeling, where you talk, but it doesn't matter, and you listen, but they're talking AT you, and your choices do NOT matter. 

Some may like it, I wanted to, but this was a big missed opportunity for me.

I am not entirely sure why this game is as highly reviewed as it is. Don't get it wrong, the art is incredible, and I love a good pixel art game. But the characters are just wildly unlikeable thus far, and while it is tagged as conversational and a visual novel, the store advertised it as having much more game play than just "select three ingredients and hope they don't get mad at you over nothing"
Maybe it's just coming to this game years after it's release, maybe it's just personal taste, but over all, not something I'd recommend, or at least, not something I enjoyed
One of the songs is actively grating. The writing is boring. Making drinks is not as interactive as VA-11 Hall-A. Couldn't get into it unfortunately

And maybe it's because I couldn't engage with the story in any meaningful way, but I found the writing BORING.

I'm honestly devastated. I've heard such amazing things about the game and I wanted to fall in love with it too. But yikes friends, this ain't it.

It looks like my opinion of this game is pretty unpopular... I do always wish for indie games with a lot of heart and effort put into them to succeed (so I'm happy this game did well!), but unfortunately I didn't enjoy it. 
The writing is the main focus of Coffee Talk, and in my opinion it's... pretty bad. It feels like a non-native English speaker wrote it. It has a lot of unnatural sentences and straight up mistakes at times. Some of the characters came across as unlikeable to me when it clearly wasn't the intention behind them. 
Like I said, this game has clear effort and heart put into it, and if the writing was something I could just brush off, it would be a perfectly fine game. But because it's the main focus I just can't.

Boring dialogues
Poor gameplay

As much as it's called Coffee Talks, sadly, the game didn't speak to me much. The only thing it did was try and serve me a "depresso," which felt stale and lacking in depth of flavor. The characters are well-designed and appealing, as is most of the game's art. However, when it comes down to actual gameplay or story, the game is subpar.

The game has its aesthetics down visually and musically, though the music is such generic coffee house music that it never really stands out. It fits the vibe I felt they were going for and thus performs its role, I guess.
Overall, this game isn't very long and can't muster up anything of greater interest or connect you with its characters within that time. As much as it pretends some of them are your regular customers, who you are already well-acquainted with, it falls short.

I'd pass on this game and recommend trying out VA-11 HALL-A instead, as it is similar in concept but far better in execution.

I agree with some here that the game is incredibly boring. You barely interact, and the interaction you get to make is frustrating and unrewarding. The Latte art game-play element is so poorly designed and hard to control, and characters do not react to it or even give any feedback whether you did it or not- not even a gallery to save your creations, simply a meaningless game-play element, why even have it? I've been waiting so long for something to happen in the game or in the story, but it gives me nothing. It's built on boring stereotypes and the political statements they are trying to make are so bland and old, all it's saying is prejudice = bad... Come on!

Welp, that was underwhelming to say the least. I got this game with perhaps (too) high hopes - ever since playing Strange Horticulture I've been looking for games in a vaguely similar vein and this one got mentioned on the interwebs a lot + has so many positive reviews, so when it was at a half price sale, I thought to myself - I might as well try. 

Well, reader, I did not think it was worth it. The play time I currently have is ca. 4 hours, at least some of which will have been from trying to gain some achievements outside of the normal gameplay time, which I'd estimate to be maybe 3, 3.5 hours. 
So it is a short game, a very short game in fact. And not only is it short, I did become bored enough each time that the 4 hours were collated across 3-4 different game play sessions? 

Having very linear + predictable stories, with very little ability to change anything (as in the only choice you can make is whether to serve someone the drink they requested or something else) and absolutely loveless writing (which honestly, is the thing that could've knocked this out of the park, but instead rammed it further into the ground, because the writing was poor. Short sentences, simple grammar, no differences in character voices, still full of stereotypes, but not in the way they wanted to draw attention to, I don't think..? - if it wasn't written in English, maybe this is at its root a translation issue, rather than the entire writing, but in English the experience remains poor). 
Coffee making can be frustrating, and it is far less of a puzzle aspect than I would like (or that I guessed it might be, based on what others said). It also seems to have rather less of an effect on story telling, than would make it interesting, because there's barely any narrative... 

[h3]tl;dr[/h3]: if you enjoy short, on the nose stories that are cozy and uplifting with at best middling writing and playing around with coffee/tea/flavour combinations, this might be the game for you. If you enjoy more or less mindlessly producing these variations, again very great, chill, game for that. 

So far, it's really not been the game for me, unfortunately, and that's why it is getting a thumb down for the moment.

Welp, seems like I'm in the tiny minority who did not enjoy this game.

I saw people praising it and since I was looking for something short and cozy for a change, I got it when it was on sale. However, whatever all the people who have left positive reviews saw in this game was clearly lost on me.

First, there were no options to pick when it came to dialogue which frustrated me a lot. I get this is a visual novel but I would've wanted to have at least some sort of options to choose from, now it was simply clicking and clicking and clicking while reading dialogue which I could not take any part of in any meaningful way. There are visual novels that offer you choices and I was expecting that from Coffee Talk as well but was sorely disappointed.

Second, the stories to me were simply boring and really did nothing for me so reading through all that stuff was just painful. And here's the thing: I do not not mind reading when it comes to video games. At all. Some of my favourite games ever have massive amounts of reading to be done, so it is not about reading just not being my thing. I probably wouldn't have even minded not having any dialogue options to choose from that much if only the stories were actually interesting enough and written in a way that captivated me, but none of that happened here. I was actually waiting for the game to end because I just wanted it to be over already so I could go and play something else and that tells enough I think.

Third, the coffee making itself was too simple. Just mix three ingredients together and that's it. And even if I got an order wrong which happened a few times, there weren't any consequences, as far as I could tell anyway. Granted, I did not go into this game with the coffee making aspect as my main interest anyway, but since the stories weren't engaging to me and the lack of dialogue options bothered me as well, I hoped at least the coffee making would be interesting. You know, because this game is about a coffee shop. But it was not. 

So, long story short, not a game I can recommend, personally.

We tried this as it seemed like a nice cozy / chill game to play on the sofa in the evening. The vibe looked very promising but we were expecting interesting stories and unfortunately the content was just incredibly boring. It's mostly just mundane dialogue between coffee shop patrons about their daily lives. If that's your cup of tea (or coffee) then you might like this game, but I suspect you could hear more interesting stories just by sitting in a real coffee shop and listening to small talk.

There's also no gameplay other than selecting three ingredients to make the cup of coffee you're asked for, it's purely dialogue-driven.

We read for about 30 minutes or so, progressively skimming as it became obvious it wasn't going to get more interesting, and then gave up and got a refund.

P.S. Play Midnight Ramen instead, it's the answer to the question "what if Coffee Talk were more interesting?"

Coffee Talk is pretty decent overall. The art style and music is a wonderful fit for the atmosphere the game tries to provide and I do not hate the world Coffee Talk is trying to build. While the concept of fantasy in the context of realism is not a new one, the game at its core is a visual novel. Unfortunately, as a visual novel, the writing of the game is its main vehicle for exposition as well as its biggest failure. Dialogue between characters is awkward and lack distinction. It sounds as if a single voice is speaking through different masks which is not desirable especially for a game that promises variety in its characters. And if that isn't bad enough, there are so many weird and frankly, unacceptable grammatical errors. So yeah. Good idea, but it requires refinement. 

3.5/10

The general themes and aesthetics of this game are really nice, I like the premise of making coffee and hearing people's stories. However, the story feels weak at times, boring even. I was rather disappointed in the queer baiting that happened. They include characters with obvious romances but the only love story's that happen are the hetero ones, and the story's revolving around queer relationships are not touched on. They were too afraid it seems to have even mentioned the queer relationships that were alluded to. The only character in the story that was of other gender was made an alien who didn't understand how gender functioned as a role at all, which made it all feel very numb to me. Disappointing to say the least.

Kinda disappointed. Thought this would be right up my alley and it probably would've been but the writing was more juvenile than I expected. Really gave "video game writing" as in kinda forced and not really natural. On top of that, moralistic and heavy-handed in a way that gave "this is for a very specific audience whose world-view needs to stay cozy and innocent". Itty-bitty babies that need to be protected. Which is odd considering the mature conversations clearly intended for an adult audience. It should be of no surprise then that my favourite character was Hyde. Another thing that kinda sucked was that I thought this would be more of a barista simulator than it actually was. I thought these conversations would happen in between or threaded through a constant stream of bustling customers. And that the drinks would effect the environment more than they actually did. So the combination of the unpleasant writing and the fact that this isn't a barista sim made this basically a visual novel with a really tedious time travel loop. 

Actually upon second thought, I'm really disappointed. Especially since none of this improves with the second game (thought I'd get it to give it chance, as I tend to do with indies). Would rate 2 out of 5. 

NOTE: The game entirely relies on reading so half my gripes would be fixed if the writers sorted out the juxtaposition in tone. Why are we having adult conversations in tones written for children, and why are we telling adults (the intended audience for the game, I presume, considering the subject matter of some of these conversations) what to think in a game that's supposed to be "deep" and "philosophical". There's no abstraction. Every character is a mouth piece for the same message and there's no real room to think. (An even worse problem in the second game.)
fun enough, but the dialogue can be very mid/therapizing which i guess is somewhat the point? but also the latte art is hard haha
